research_question: Does ultrasound-based radiomics provide incremental predictive value beyond clinical and conventional ultrasound models?
poolability_reason: The two pCR studies form an endpoint-aligned subgroup, but their radiomics timepoint roles differ (pretreatment baseline vs pretreatment+midpoint longitudinal), as do validation settings (internal holdout vs internal and external center validation). No sufficiently aligned subgroup remains for quantitative pooling; no forest plot or meta-analysis was produced.
key_message: High predictive performance does not by itself demonstrate incremental value.
synthesis: All four reports provide predictive performance, but outcome definitions and imaging strategies differ.
Yang 2022 targets an imaging-defined RECIST response, not pCR; its delta score was not significantly better than the baseline or early score in the reported comparison.
Wang 2025 reports Miller–Payne MHR (G4–G5), not pCR; its validation combined-model AUC is reported approximately and remains flagged for exact-value review.

The two pCR studies report promising combined-model performance, but the 2024 study's internal validation AUC is lower than training; Wu 2025 uses pretreatment plus midpoint imaging and has an abstract/table discrepancy for external fusion AUC.
Comparisons do not establish a consistent incremental contribution of radiomics beyond a conventional ultrasound/clinical model across all four studies.
limitations: Four selected studies only; not an exhaustive systematic review.
Several extraction values and timing details are ambiguous or approximate and remain flagged.
No pooling was run; qualitative poolability judgment is not a meta-analysis.
